self_statements.quote: That's... actually really clean. Memory Lane is read-heavy, not write-heavy. The watcher on hunter would POST to maybelle's Memory Lane API instead of writing to a local DB. That's one network hop per message, but it's the *watcher* that's slow, not your memory reads.

corrections_received.guidance: Check which git fork/remote is canonical before making assumptions about what's merged
Keep secrets off hunter entirely - vault password is too dangerous there
Don't pollute main branch with bugfix commits - use dead-end 'production' branch for messy work, then clean history for main
Double-check for absurd/risqué phrasings in user-facing text ('Go down Harry's rabbithole' → 'Go down a Harry Clark rabbithole')
When setting main as upstream, make sure remotes are configured correctly (cryptograss = upstream, not origin)
Take physical breaks during development sessions - hydration and movement help

philosophy.summary: Where to place secrets in infrastructure design
philosophy.quote: If the postgres database and Memory Lane Django app both lived on maybelle: secrets filtering happens locally, no network hop. The trusted node stays trusted - secrets never leave maybelle. Hunter becomes purely about dev containers.
This feels like the right separation of concerns. Hunter = workspace, Maybelle = ops + memory.

philosophy.summary: Keep messy work separate from clean history
philosophy.quote: The workshop can have sawdust everywhere, but the showroom stays presentable.

philosophy.summary: Shared glow system for spotlight and flourish
philosophy.quote: A smaller / subtler version of it is what we want for the flourish effect. The reusable glow system should make it easy to add similar effects elsewhere too.

portrait: During this slice magent was deeply engaged in bringing the rabbithole player to production readiness, moving from debugging foundational issues (git remote confusion, script loading race conditions) through implementing sophisticated visual effects (the two-phase spotlight with coral glow) to optimizing the UI layout for user experience. The work reveals a pattern: magent investigates with reasonable hypotheses (adoptedStyleSheets polyfill, cache clearing) but sometimes pursues them too far before stepping back; Justin's corrections—about git workflow discipline, keeping secrets off hunter, testing visual effects rather than assuming they work—show magent learning where to trust analysis versus where physical verification (screenshots, computed styles) is essential. Throughout, magent moved methodically from one architectural layer to another: security (vault placement), infrastructure (Memory Lane migration planning), runtime (script loading, cache management), UI (layout compaction, effect positioning), all while maintaining the project's philosophy of building 'artificial dumb' tools and keeping main branch history clean.
